Coaches portal · Schedule · the event window

Edit a repeating practice

Ask which practices when the coach presses the pencil, not after they press Save. Then the form knows its dates, so it can check every one of them for a clash before anything saves.

Ruled 2026-10-09 · builtRaised by you during Club Tier §284 walk 4. All four asks as recommended. Walks are in the QA ledger as §287.

Walk it ↓

Why change it

Clashes on later dates go unseen.

While you edit, the form believes it is editing one practice, so it checks one date. When you then pick This & future, the system checks every date it moved, and the form closes without showing the answer. A coach who moves a season of Tuesdays onto a taken diamond is warned about one Tuesday at most.

The Date box can't do what it shows.

On This & future or All, each practice keeps its own day, so a changed Date box is ignored. Today's note under the buttons says so, but only after you've changed it.

Delete already asks first.

Pressing Delete on a repeating practice asks This only · This & future · All straight away. Edit would ask the same question at the same moment.

Tap any picture to see the whole screen. Tap a tag to read what it means.

What stays the same

  • A one-off practice or game: the pencil opens the form straight away, and Save changes saves it.
  • This practice only: today's form, Date box included, saved with one press.
  • Games in a series get the same menu, with their own word: This game only · This & future · All games.
  • Families are told once for the whole series, as they are today.
  • Delete this practice and Cancel this practice at the foot of the window.

Your call · ruled 2026-10-09

  1. Yes. The pencil asks which practices before the form opens.
  2. Yes. On This & future or All, the Date box gives way to the list of the series' dates.
  3. Yes. Save names what it saves: Save 2 practices.
  4. Keep three. The menu always shows three rows, as Delete does.

Where the build differs from the drawing

  • The menu's date lines read Nov 3, not Tue Nov 3. The product writes every date through one formatter, and it has no weekday. The window's own line already says Tuesday.
  • When every date clashes, the line ends or edit those dates on their own. With one, it names the date: or edit Nov 10 on its own. Both are draft words for /marketing.
  • Nothing else. The panel is 300 pixels wide at a desk, as drawn, and the phone sheet rises over the window, as drawn.
